title: Remove post id from the 404 error body in get_post
description: Verified: flaskr/blog.py:52 — abort(404, f"Post id {id} doesn't exist.") echoes the requested post id back into the response body. While low impact (ids are sequential and non-secret here), it is a verbose error that reflects user-controlled input into the error page and diverges from the generic-error norm. Corroborates assertions.md §3 S7 (Info/Low). Not tracked by any existing feature.json.
notes: Resolved 2026-07-03: replaced abort(404, f"Post id {id} doesn't exist.") at flaskr/blog.py:75 with a generic abort(404), so the requested id is no longer reflected into the 404 error body. Confirmed tests/test_blog.py::test_exists_required asserts only status_code == 404 (no body/id assertion), so it still passes. Also hardened the source spec: blog-post-management/feature.json spec point 6 now requires the 404 abort to be generic and forbids interpolating the id, preventing reintroduction on a feature-based rebuild.
spec:
1. In flaskr/blog.py get_post, replace abort(404, f"Post id {id} doesn't exist.") at line 52 with a generic abort(404) (or a static message that does not interpolate the id).
2. Confirm tests/test_blog.py::test_exists_required still passes — it asserts a 404 status, not the body text; verify it does not assert on the id string before changing.
Note: written against the current Flask app; carry the same generic-error rule forward under a Q2 stack port.

IMPORTANT: After resolving this finding, locate the feature.json file(s) in .aidd/features/ whose spec originally produced the code or pattern that caused this audit finding. Update those feature.json spec(s) to prevent this issue from being reintroduced during a feature-based rebuild.
